title: Cost Gateway: region bucketing, accelerator selection, and graceful fallback
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Customers run inference across multiple regions and instance classes. Without tenant-level gating we see unpredictable spend spikes when spot pools evaporate or queuing shifts to on-demand SKUs. Existing routing picks by latency and raw capacity which can blow past tenant spend expectations.

Goal: Build a lightweight 'cost gateway' that enforces per-tenant soft and hard budget caps while steering inference to cheaper region buckets and preferred GPU classes. Provide deterministic degradation paths that fall back to quantified, lower-cost model variants (e.g., 8-bit/quantized or smaller sharded variants) and controlled on-demand use when spot is unavailable. The feature must be plumbed into the existing smart router and provide observability and override controls in Console.
proposal: Introduce a Cost Gateway layer between policy evaluation and scheduler allocation. Key components: (1) Region Buckets: group regions into cost tiers (e.g., cheap-spot, stable-on-demand, premium-low-latency) per-tenant budget profile. (2) Accelerator Scoring: score available accelerator classes (A100, H100, L4, T4 equivalents) by cost-per-token and expected tail-latency under current load. (3) Soft/Hard Caps: enforce per-tenant hourly soft caps allowing limited overage with throttling penalties and hard caps that reject or downgrade requests. (4) Model Variant Fallbacks: map heavy variants to cheaper quantized variants if allocation would exceed soft cap or if only spot pools remain. (5) Telemetry and circuit breakers: metrics surfaced to Console and automatic throttle when error or spend anomalies detected.
design_decisions: Region bucketing is tenant-configurable; default buckets are inferred from historical spend and latency profiles
Soft cap triggers a probabilistic throttle (p-drop) to smooth spikes rather than immediate hard rejections
Accelerator scoring combines normalized cost-per-token and empirical tail latency; we prefer stable on-demand for latency-sensitive tenants
Model variant mapping is configured in model catalog with explicit fallback chains; runtime performs version-compatible validation before fallback
Gateway is stateless for decision-making; stateful counters live in Redis with per-tenant keys to minimize coordination latency
implementation_notes: Add CostGateway service next to Router (pkg/costgateway) with a lightweight API: Evaluate(tenant, request_meta) -> Decision{region_bucket, accelerator_class, variant, action}
Extend tenant config (db/tenants) with cost_profile: {soft_hourly_usd, hard_hourly_usd, preferred_regions, bucket_overrides}
Integrate with scheduler by returning preference scores; scheduler retains final placement but honors hard caps by rejecting allocations that would exceed counters
Add migration to populate default cost_profile using last-90-days spend and median latency (migrations/2026_02_cost_gateway_defaults.sql)

Config example (Console) to expose per-tenant soft cap slider and per-model fallback mapping: 
  - soft_hourly_usd: 120.00
  - hard_hourly_usd: 180.00
  - model_fallbacks: ["model-x:quant8-v1", "model-x:small-v2"]
Telemetry: emit events 'costgateway.decision' and 'costgateway.cap_violation' with tags {tenant, region_bucket, accelerator_class, variant, decision_reason} to tracing and metrics
acceptance_criteria: API: CostGateway Evaluate API returns deterministic decisions for identical inputs in 99.9% of calls
Budget enforcement: soft cap reduces token spend growth by >= 40% during synthetic spike tests without exceeding hard cap during 24h window
Fallback correctness: when fallback triggered, SDK clients receive structured hint for variant with stable schema and no corruption of KV cache
Latency SLA: median token latency remains within 1.2x baseline for tenants who allow quantized fallbacks; 95th percentile increase limited to 1.5x
Observability: Console shows per-tenant spent vs cap and a drill-down list of gateway decisions; alerts fire on cap_violation events
test_plan: Unit tests for scoring function with synthetic cost and latency distributions
Integration harness: run multi-tenant simulation with mixed spot eviction patterns and measure spend smoothing versus control (no gateway)
E2E: staged rollout on dedicated canary fleet for 48 hours with opt-in tenants, compare error rate and p95 latency
Chaos test: simulate spot pool loss in a region and validate gateway triggers variant fallback chains and prevents hard cap breaches
Security review: ensure tenant config propagation cannot be used to escalate resource priority
risks: Overly aggressive throttling may degrade UX for high-value tenants—need conservative defaults and per-tenant tuning
Incorrect model variant substitution could cause semantic regressions; require eval pass and approval in model catalog
State synchronization errors could cause double-counting of spend; mitigate with idempotent counter increments and reconciliation job
Telemetry volume from decision events could increase metrics cost—sample non-critical events by default
